criterion: M3 lighting (dated addition 7, 2026-10-10): punctual lights in physical units, clustered light assignment, image-based lighting
written: 2026-10-10, before the implementation and the first run

model.units: Lights follow KHR_lights_punctual: directional in lux, point and spot in candela, spot cones with the specification's smooth falloff, and its recommended range window clamp(1 - (d/range)^4, 0, 1)^2 / d^2 (no range: 1 / d^2). Emission is in nits. A physical camera gives EV100 = log2(N^2 / t * 100 / S) and exposure 1 / (1.2 * 2^EV100) (Lagarde and de Rousiers 2014).
model.clusters: View-space froxels: 16 x 9 screen tiles by 24 depth slices, exponential in depth between near and far. A light is listed in a cluster when its range sphere meets the cluster's view-space bounding box (Arvo's sphere-box test). Up to 128 lights a cluster; an overflow counter records any cut.
model.ibl: Split sum (Karis 2013): specular = prefiltered(r) * (f0 A + f90 B), plus the materials' own multiple-scattering lobe integrated against the irradiance, Kms * (1 - E(mu_o)) * irradiance; A, B, E and Kms come from raw::pbr::Tables and the material model, so the DFG term is not a second fit and direct and image lighting share one energy model. Layers under IBL: the dielectric base weighted by (1 - E_s(mu_o)), the clearcoat as a second split-sum lobe with what is below weighted by (1 - c E_c(mu_o))^2, sheen as sheenColor * E_sh(mu_o) * irradiance, transmission sampling the prefiltered environment along the transmitted direction. The prefiltered environment is a cube map stored in a buffer, GGX importance sampled per roughness level with the N = V = R assumption; diffuse uses the irradiance from order-2 spherical harmonics of the environment (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan 2001). The test environment is procedural (a sky gradient, a ground and a sun disk), so no image asset enters the repository.

units.what: a white Lambertian surface facing a point light of I candela at distance d, a directional light of E lux, and a spot light on and off its cone
units.bound: radiance equals rho/pi * I/d^2, rho/pi * E and the falloff formulas within 1e-12 relative; exposure equals the EV100 formula within 1e-12

ibl_furnace.what: a uniform environment of radiance L0 and a white metal at roughness 0.05 to 1 by 0.05, view cosine 0.05 to 1 by 0.05, through the split-sum path

ibl_split_sum_error.what: the split-sum path against importance-sampled integration of the full material (raw::pbr::eval) over the same procedural environment, 2,048 seeded samples of normal, view, roughness 0.1 to 1 and metal or dielectric, where the reference exceeds 1% of the environment's mean radiance
ibl_split_sum_error.bound: relative error of luminance: median <= 5%, 95th percentile <= 20% (the split sum is an approximation; this records how good it is)

cluster_no_miss.what: 8 seeded scenes of 256 point and spot lights with random ranges, 65,536 seeded view-space points inside the frustum
cluster_no_miss.bound: zero lights with a nonzero contribution at a point missing from that point's cluster list (on the CPU lists and on the GPU lists)

cluster_gpu_equal.what: the GPU's cluster lists against the CPU's, same scenes
cluster_gpu_equal.bound: identical sets in every cluster, except lights whose sphere-box distance is within 1e-4 of the range (float32 boundary cases), which are counted and reported

cluster_shading_equal.what: shading a point from its cluster list against shading it from all lights, same points
cluster_shading_equal.bound: |clustered - brute force| <= 1e-6 |brute force| (the same lights in the same order)

gpu_parity.what: a WGSL pass shades 4,096 seeded surface samples (position, normal, view, material over every family) with clustered punctual lights and the split-sum IBL, in float32, against the float64 reference of the same lights, clusters and prefiltered environment; values are exposed (multiplied by the exposure) so they sit near 1
gpu_parity.bound: |gpu - ref| <= 2e-3 |ref| + 1e-5 on every channel, on D3D12 WARP and on WebGPU (SwiftShader in Chrome)

prefilter_parity.what: the GPU prefilter pass against the CPU prefilter, every texel of every roughness level of a 32 x 32 face cube

controls.what: the GPU shading with lights dropped from the cluster lists at random, and the GPU prefilter with the sample count halved

does_not_prove: That area lights are right (a later slice); that shadows are right (none are cast here); that frames from the scene renderer are right (this checks shading on samples, not rasterized frames); performance on any GPU; that the procedural environment stands for photographed ones.
